- Model tends to overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Overshoots occur frequently after sharp upward moves in the history, leading to inflated forecasts that fail to account for mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true values show a downward trend or consolidation.
- Forecast bias is often positive in the first 10–15 days, then shifts to negative or flat in later days — suggesting a lag in adjusting to recent price action.
- Model fails to capture short-term volatility clustering; it smooths out sharp swings, leading to underestimation of true price volatility.
- When true values show a clear upward trend, model often overreacts with a premature peak, then underestimates the continuation.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in the middle of the forecast, especially when history shows a strong upward momentum.
- Correction should involve reducing forecast magnitude by 5–15% for the last 5–10 days if true values show downward pressure or consolidation.
- Model should adjust downward after a spike in history, especially if the spike is followed by a correction — avoid “overcorrection” or “undercorrection” in the same direction.
